articles.detail: 5 cycles, 5 completed; 11/11/13/15/13 stories went to the writer against targets of 11/12/13/15/15; 6 quarantined for having no dateline and no location

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active and no pause gate is set. The one goal that slipped, science plus tech at 24%, was caused by the validator quarantining six written science and tech articles, not by supply or selection; with them the day is 19 of 60, or 32%. No tunable parameter reaches that, so there is nothing to test.
weakestArea: Science plus tech is 24% against 25%, and science is 4 against 5, because six articles were quarantined as 'no dateline and no location': three science (biodiversity, the dog Alzheimer's study, the early flu season) and three tech (counterfeit TLS certificates, VMware licensing, OpenAI watermarking). In the 10:00, 14:00 and 22:00 cycles the writer left the dateline and location off placeless stories, in two cycles citing the selection angles, and the validator requires both. Yesterday had no quarantines.
watching: Saudi Arabia: Pakistan and Turkey are to deploy troops under the Mecca pact, which was the day's breaking-news push.
Yemen: fighting around Mokha and Jazan continues, and the 22:00 cycle's only multi-source story was a Yemen entry the selector merged by hand.
Hormuz: the International Chamber of Commerce's forecast of grain prices up as much as 80% was passed over as one official's estimate; Saudi discounts are pulling against the war premium on oil.
Russia: the Irkutsk plague case now has a local report of up to 200 people quarantined while the health watchdog calls the diagnosis unconfirmed.
Kenya: authorities are tracing 27 passengers from a flight linked to an Ebola case.
Bank of Japan: sources say it may signal underlying inflation has reached its 2% goal.
Lithuania: parliament voted to remove its ban on nuclear weapons, sourced to state media alone.
ASML's share move went unexplained by the feed for a third day; the only item was a thin analyst-note teaser.
The Port Shuaiba drone attack trended in the 14:00 and 18:00 cycles with nothing in the feed to cover it.
coverageGaps: Six science and tech articles were written and then quarantined for lacking a dateline and location, which cost science 3 of 7 and tech 3 of 12.

Latin America had two datelines (Puerto Tejada and Madre de Dios), 4% against 5%; two thin Bloomberg picks taken for the region at 22:00, on Codelco and the Panama Canal, were dropped when the page fetch returned under 400 characters.
Economy was under its floor after dedup in three of five cycles (1, 2 and 2 against 3) and ended the day at 10, down from 17.
Economy had no native multi-source pick at 18:00 or 22:00, and politics had none at 22:00, when the feed carried three multi-source clusters.
Science was at zero in the 05:00 cycle and one at 18:00; the selector found nothing from Quanta, STAT, SciDev.Net or Carbon Brief in either feed.
Tech was two short at 10:00, when the feed had no Ars Technica, 404 Media, Register, Decoder or Hacker News items.
Thin picks were recovered for 3 of 8 sources across the day; every failure that named an outlet was Bloomberg.
Europe carried 21 of 54 datelines and Asia 5, down from 10 yesterday.
Freshness could not be measured: the metric counted 0 of 54 articles today, after 2 of 62 yesterday.
context: All five cycles completed in an average of 893s (selector 185s, writer 197s, editor 80s). The quarantine is the operator's item: the dateline gate in validate-articles.js is doing what it was built for, but placeless science and tech stories are reaching it with no location, and the fix sits in the prompts or the validator, outside what the tuner may edit. Multi-source held at 37% and US datelines at 24% with the per-cycle cap of three reached in three cycles; odds rows were offered in two cycles (3 rows).
